notes:
OWASP A03 stored-XSS surface verified clean. The Telegram-rendered string (response.rendered) is output EXCLUSIVELY as text via Vue {{ }} interpolation at FunnelMessagePreview.vue:149 (
{{ rendered.rendered }}
), which HTML-escapes by default; line breaks are preserved via CSS whitespace-pre-wrap, not markup. Grep over both new/modified files (FunnelMessagePreview.vue, [funnelId].vue) finds v-html/innerHTML only inside source comments — no actual sink, and no outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/dangerouslySet anywhere. The 'no v-html' vitest assertion is genuine: it feeds payload 'x', asserts the literal string is present in textContent AND that rendered.find('img')/find('b')/querySelector('img') are absent (proving text node, not DOM injection), plus a static source guard that strips comments before matching /v-html\s*=/ and /\.innerHTML\s*=/. All 7 component tests pass. Non-message placeholder, sample-data indicator, and the toggle label are i18n keys (funnels.editor.previewPlaceholder / previewSampleData / preview), present in both en.json and uk.json (lines 719-721) — no raw server string injected as HTML. Error state is mapped through useApiError, which resolves ONLY from i18n 'errors.*' keys via te()/t() and never echoes the raw server error body, so the error path is not a sink either. sampleData/stub values are backend-controlled neutral strings rendered through the same text-only path. No A03 (or other OWASP) issue found; approved.
